before.answer: ## প্ৰশ্ন 19 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.39 ত, $\triangle PQR$ ৰ QP বাহুক S বিন্দুলৈ বঢ়াই দিয়া হৈছে, আৰু RQ বাহুক T বিন্দুলৈ বঢ়াই দিয়া হৈছে। যদি $\angle SPR=135°$ আৰু $\angle PQT=110°$, তেন্তে $\angle PRQ$ নিৰ্ণয় কৰা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** $\angle SPR+\angle RPQ=180°$ (P ত ৰৈখিক যোৰ): $$135°+\angle RPQ=180° \implies \angle RPQ=180°-135°$$ **$\angle RPQ=45°$** আমি জানো ত্ৰিভুজৰ বহিঃকোণ ইয়াৰ পৰা দূৰত থকা দুটা অন্তঃকোণৰ যোগফলৰ সমান। $\angle PQT$ হৈছে Q ত থকা বহিঃকোণ: $$\angle PQT=\angle RPQ+\angle PRQ$$ $$110°=45°+\angle PRQ \implies \angle PRQ=110°-45°$$ **$\angle PRQ=65°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 20 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.40 ত, $\angle X=62°$, $\angle XYZ=54°$। যদি $\triangle XYZ$ ৰ YO আৰু ZO ক্ৰমে $\angle XYZ$ আৰু $\angle XZY$ ৰ সমদ্বিখণ্ডক, তেন্তে $\angle OZY$ আৰু $\angle YOZ$ উলিওৱা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** $\triangle XYZ$ ত: $\angle X+\angle XYZ+\angle XZY=180°$: $$62°+54°+\angle XZY=180° \implies \angle XZY=180°-116°=64°$$ ZO এ $\angle XZY$ ক সমদ্বিখণ্ডিত কৰে: $$\angle XZO=\angle OZY=\dfrac12\angle XZY=\dfrac12\times64°=32°$$ **$\angle OZY=32°$** YO এ $\angle XYZ$ ক সমদ্বিখণ্ডিত কৰে: $\angle XYO=\angle OYZ=\dfrac12\times54°=27°$। $\triangle OYZ$ ত: $$\angle OYZ+\angle YOZ+\angle OZY=180°$$ $$27°+\angle YOZ+32°=180° \implies \angle YOZ=180°-59°$$ **$\angle YOZ=121°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 21 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.41 ত, যদি $AB \parallel DE$, $\angle BAC=35°$ আৰু $\angle CDE=53°$, তেন্তে $\angle DCE$ উলিওৱা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** $AB \parallel DE$, AE ছেদক (A, C, E একে ৰেখাত): $$\angle BAC=\angle DEC=35° \quad (\text{একান্তৰ অন্তঃকোণ})$$ এতিয়া, $\triangle CDE$ ত: $$\angle DCE+\angle CDE+\angle DEC=180°$$ $$\angle DCE+53°+35°=180° \implies \angle DCE+88°=180°$$ **$\angle DCE=92°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 22 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.42 ত, PQ আৰু RS ৰেখা দুডালে T বিন্দুত পৰস্পৰক ছেদ কৰিছে, যাতে $\angle PRT=40°$, $\angle RPT=95°$ আৰু $\angle TSQ=75°$, তেন্তে $\angle SQT$ উলিওৱা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** $\triangle PRT$ ত: $\angle PRT+\angle RPT+\angle RTP=180°$: $$40°+95°+\angle RTP=180° \implies \angle RTP=180°-135°$$ **$\angle RTP=45°$** $\angle RTP$ আৰু $\angle STQ$ বিপ্ৰতীপ কোণ (PQ আৰু RS T ত ছেদ কৰে): $$\angle RTP=\angle STQ=45°$$ $\triangle STQ$ ত: $\angle STQ+\angle TSQ+\angle SQT=180°$: $$45°+75°+\angle SQT=180° \implies \angle SQT=180°-120°$$ **$\angle SQT=60°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 23 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.43 ত, যদি $PQ \perp PS$, $PQ \parallel SR$, $\angle SQR=28°$ আৰু $\angle QRT=65°$, তেন্তে $x$ আৰু $y$ ৰ মান উলিওৱা। *(3 নম্বৰ — কঠিন)* **উত্তৰ** $PQ \perp PS \implies \angle SPQ=90°$। যিহেতু $PQ \parallel SR$ আৰু QS ছেদক: $$x=\angle QSR \quad (\text{একান্তৰ অন্তঃকোণ, য'ত } x=\angle PQS)$$ দিয়া আছে $\angle SQR=28°$, $\angle QRT=65°$। $\triangle QSR$ ত, $\angle QRT$ R ত থকা বহিঃকোণ, যিটো ইয়াৰ পৰা দূৰত থকা দুটা অন্তঃকোণৰ যোগফলৰ সমান: $$\angle QSR+\angle SQR=\angle QRT$$ $$\angle QSR+28°=65° \implies \angle QSR=65°-28°=37°$$ **$x=\angle QSR=37°$** $\triangle SPQ$ ত: $\angle SPQ+\angle PQS+\angle PSQ=180°$: $$90°+x+y=180° \implies 90°+37°+y=180° \implies 127°+y=180°$$ **$y=53°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 24 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.44 ত, $\triangle PQR$ ৰ QR বাহুক S বিন্দুলৈ বঢ়াই দিয়া হ'ল। $\angle PQR$ আৰু $\angle PRS$ ৰ সমদ্বিখণ্ডক দুডাল T বিন্দুত মিলিত হয়। তেন্তে প্ৰমাণ কৰা যে $\angle QTR=\dfrac12\angle QPR$। *(5 নম্বৰ — কঠিন)* **উত্তৰ** আমি জানো ত্ৰিভুজৰ বহিঃকোণ ইয়াৰ পৰা দূৰত থকা দুটা অন্তঃকোণৰ যোগফলৰ সমান। $\triangle PQR$ ত, $\angle PRS$ হৈছে R ত থকা বহিঃকোণ: $$\angle PRS=\angle QPR+\angle PQR$$ দুয়োফাল আধা কৰি: $$\dfrac12\angle PRS=\dfrac12\angle QPR+\dfrac12\angle PQR$$ যিহেতু RT এ $\angle PRS$ ক সমদ্বিখণ্ডিত কৰে ($\angle TRS=\dfrac12\angle PRS$) আৰু QT এ $\angle PQR$ ক সমদ্বিখণ্ডিত কৰে ($\angle TQR=\dfrac12\angle PQR$): $$\angle TRS=\dfrac12\angle QPR+\angle TQR \qquad ...(i)$$ এতিয়া, $\triangle TQR$ ত, $\angle TRS$ হৈছে R ত থকা বহিঃকোণ: $$\angle TRS=\angle QTR+\angle TQR \qquad ...(ii)$$ (i) আৰু (ii) ৰ পৰা: $$\angle QTR+\angle TQR=\dfrac12\angle QPR+\angle TQR$$ **$\therefore\ \angle QTR=\dfrac12\angle QPR$ — প্ৰমাণিত।**

## Question 11 **Question:** In Fig. 6.28, find the values of $x$ and $y$, and then show that $AB \parallel CD$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** From Fig. 6.28: $$50°+x°=180° \quad (\text{linear pair at X})$$ $$\implies x=180-50$$ **$x=130°$** Also, $y=130°$ (since $y$ and the given $130°$ angle at Y are vertically opposite angles). **$x=y=130°$** Since $x=y=130°$ are equal alternate interior angles formed by the transversal with AB and CD: **$\therefore\ AB \parallel CD$** --- ## Question 12 **Question:** In Fig. 6.29, if $AB \parallel CD$, $CD \parallel EF$ and $y:z=3:7$, find $x$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** Given $y:z=3:7$. Let $y=3k$, $z=7k$. Let $p$ be the angle vertically opposite to $y$ at the same point, so $p=y$. Now, $p+z=180°$ (co-interior angles on the same side of the transversal, since $AB \parallel EF$ via CD): $$y+z=180° \implies 3k+7k=180° \implies 10k=180° \implies k=18°$$ $$\therefore\ y=3k°=3\times18°=54°$$ Also, $x+y=180°$ (co-interior angles on the same side of the transversal, since $AB \parallel CD$): $$x+54°=180° \implies x=180-54$$ **$x=126°$** --- ## Question 13 **Question:** In Fig. 6.30, if $AB \parallel CD$, $EF \perp CD$ and $\angle GED=126°$, find $\angle AGE$, $\angle GEF$ and $\angle FGE$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** $AB \parallel CD$, GE is a transversal: $$\angle GED=\angle AGE=126° \quad (\text{alternate interior angles})$$ **$\angle AGE=126°$** Also, $\angle GED=\angle FED+\angle GEF$: $$126°=90°+\angle GEF \implies \angle GEF=126°-90°$$ **$\angle GEF=36°$** Also, $\angle AGE+\angle FGE=180°$ (linear pair): $$126°+\angle FGE=180° \implies \angle FGE=180°-126°$$ **$\angle FGE=54°$** --- ## Question 14 **Question:** In Fig. 6.31, $PQ \parallel ST$, $\angle PQR=110°$ and $\angle RST=130°$, find $\angle QRS$. [Hint: Draw a line through point R parallel to line ST.] *(3 Marks — Hard)* **Answer** Given: $PQ \parallel ST$, $\angle PQR=110°$, $\angle RST=130°$. Draw ray RA through R parallel to ST (and hence parallel to PQ too). Since two parallel lines cut by a transversal have co-interior angles on the same side summing to $180°$: $$\angle RST+\angle SRA=180° \implies 130°+\angle SRA=180° \implies \angle SRA=50°$$ Since $RQ \parallel ST$ and hence $RQ \parallel RA$: $QR$ is the transversal, and $$\angle PQR=\angle QRA=110° \quad (\text{alternate interior angles})$$ Now, $\angle QRS+\angle SRA=\angle QRA$: $$\angle QRS+50°=110° \implies \angle QRS=110°-50°$$ **$\angle QRS=60°$** --- ## Question 15 **Question:** In Fig. 6.32, if $AB \parallel CD$, $\angle APQ=50°$ and $\angle PRD=127°$, find $x$ and $y$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** $AB \parallel CD$, PQ is a transversal: $$x=50° \quad (\text{alternate interior angles with } \angle APQ)$$ **$x=50°$** $\angle PRD=127°$ and $\angle PRQ$ are a linear pair on line CD, so $\angle PRQ=180°-127°=53°$. In $\triangle PQR$: $$y+x+\angle PRQ=180°$$ $$y+50°+53°=180° \implies y+103°=180°$$ **$y=77°$** --- ## Question 16 **Question:** In Fig. 6.33, PQ and RS are two mirrors placed parallel to each other. An incident ray AB strikes mirror PQ at B and, after reflecting along path BC, strikes mirror RS at C. This ray then reflects again in the direction CD. Prove that $AB \parallel CD$. *(5 Marks — Hard)* **Answer** By the figure, PQ and RS are two parallel plane mirrors. Incident ray AB strikes mirror PQ at B and reflects as ray BC. Ray CD reflects from mirror RS at C. We must prove $AB \parallel CD$. We know: angle of incidence = angle of reflection. $$\therefore\ \angle 1=\angle 2 \ \text{ and } \ \angle 3=\angle 4 \qquad ...(1)$$ $\angle 1$ is the angle between incident ray AB and the normal BL; $\angle 2$ is the angle between reflected ray BC and the normal BL. Similarly $\angle 3$ and $\angle 4$ are the corresponding angles of incidence and reflection at C. Since $PQ \parallel RS$ and $BL \perp PQ$, we get $CM \perp RS$ too, so $BL \parallel CM$ (both perpendicular to a pair of parallel lines). Now, $BL \parallel CM$ with BC as transversal: $$\angle 2=\angle 3 \quad (\text{alternate interior angles}) \qquad ...(2)$$ $$\angle ABC=\angle 1+\angle 2=\angle 2+\angle 2=2\angle 2 \quad (\text{using } \angle 1=\angle 2 \text{ from (1)})$$ $$\angle BCD=\angle 3+\angle 4=\angle 3+\angle 3=2\angle 3 \quad (\text{using } \angle 3=\angle 4 \text{ from (1)})$$ But from (2), $\angle 2=\angle 3$, so $2\angle 2=2\angle 3$: $$\therefore\ \angle ABC=\angle BCD$$ $\angle ABC$ and $\angle BCD$ are alternate interior angles formed by transversal BC with lines AB-extended and CD-extended, and they are equal. **$\therefore\ AB \parallel CD$ — proved.** --- ## Question 17 **Question:** In this question, one statement is labelled Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R). Choose the correct option from the choices below: Assertion (A): If side BC of a triangle ABC is produced to point D, then $\angle ACD=\angle A+\angle B$. Reason (R): The sum of the three angles of a triangle is $180°$. (a) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A) (b) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A) (c) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false (d) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true *(1 Mark — Moderate)* **Answer** **(b) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)** Assertion (A) is the Exterior Angle Property of a triangle, which is true. Reason (R), the angle-sum property, is also true — but on its own it is not sufficient to explain (A); the linear pair $\angle ACB+\angle ACD=180°$ is also needed together with the angle-sum property to derive the exterior angle result, so (R) alone is not the complete/correct explanation of (A). --- ## Question 18 **Question:** Match Column-I with Column-II. | Column-I | Column-II | |---|---| | (A) If $x°$ and $y°$ are complementary angles and $2x=3y$, then $x=$ | (P) $45°$ | | (B) If an angle equals its own complement, then the measure of the angle is | (Q) $90°$ | | (C) If $x°$ and $y°$ form a linear pair such that $x-y=60°$, then $y=$ | (R) $60°$ | | (D) If an angle equals its own supplement, then the measure of the angle is | (S) $54°$ | Choose the correct option: (a) A→S, B→P, C→R, D→Q (b) A→Q, B→S, C→R, D→P (c) A→Q, B→P, C→S, D→R (d) A→P, B→Q, C→R, D→S *(1 Mark — Hard)* **Answer** **(a) A→S, B→P, C→R, D→Q** **(A)** $x+y=90°$ (complementary) and $2x=3y \implies y=\dfrac{2x}{3}$. So $x+\dfrac{2x}{3}=90° \implies \dfrac{5x}{3}=90° \implies x=54°$. **→ (S) $54°$** **(B)** Angle equals its own complement: $x=90°-x \implies 2x=90° \implies x=45°$. **→ (P) $45°$** **(C)** $x+y=180°$ (linear pair) and $x-y=60°$. Adding: $2x=240° \implies x=120°$; subtracting: $2y=120° \implies y=60°$. **→ (R) $60°$** **(D)** Angle equals its own supplement: $x=180°-x \implies 2x=180° \implies x=90°$. **→ (Q) $90°$** *(Note: this uses the standard convention that "complementary" angles sum to $90°$ and a "linear pair" sums to $180°$ — each sub-part above was solved independently from its own given condition, and the four results S, P, R, Q together use each option exactly once.)*

## Question 19 **Question:** In Fig. 6.39, side QP of $\triangle PQR$ is produced to point S, and side RQ is produced to point T. If $\angle SPR=135°$ and $\angle PQT=110°$, find $\angle PRQ$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** $\angle SPR+\angle RPQ=180°$ (linear pair at P): $$135°+\angle RPQ=180° \implies \angle RPQ=180°-135°$$ **$\angle RPQ=45°$** We know the exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. $\angle PQT$ is the exterior angle at Q: $$\angle PQT=\angle RPQ+\angle PRQ$$ $$110°=45°+\angle PRQ \implies \angle PRQ=110°-45°$$ **$\angle PRQ=65°$** --- ## Question 20 **Question:** In Fig. 6.40, $\angle X=62°$, $\angle XYZ=54°$. If YO and ZO are, respectively, the bisectors of $\angle XYZ$ and $\angle XZY$ of $\triangle XYZ$, find $\angle OZY$ and $\angle YOZ$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** In $\triangle XYZ$: $\angle X+\angle XYZ+\angle XZY=180°$: $$62°+54°+\angle XZY=180° \implies \angle XZY=180°-116°=64°$$ ZO bisects $\angle XZY$: $$\angle XZO=\angle OZY=\dfrac12\angle XZY=\dfrac12\times64°=32°$$ **$\angle OZY=32°$** YO bisects $\angle XYZ$: $\angle XYO=\angle OYZ=\dfrac12\times54°=27°$. In $\triangle OYZ$: $$\angle OYZ+\angle YOZ+\angle OZY=180°$$ $$27°+\angle YOZ+32°=180° \implies \angle YOZ=180°-59°$$ **$\angle YOZ=121°$** --- ## Question 21 **Question:** In Fig. 6.41, if $AB \parallel DE$, $\angle BAC=35°$ and $\angle CDE=53°$, find $\angle DCE$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** $AB \parallel DE$, AE is a transversal (through A, C, E): $$\angle BAC=\angle DEC=35° \quad (\text{alternate interior angles})$$ Now, in $\triangle CDE$: $$\angle DCE+\angle CDE+\angle DEC=180°$$ $$\angle DCE+53°+35°=180° \implies \angle DCE+88°=180°$$ **$\angle DCE=92°$** --- ## Question 22 **Question:** In Fig. 6.42, lines PQ and RS intersect each other at point T, such that $\angle PRT=40°$, $\angle RPT=95°$ and $\angle TSQ=75°$, find $\angle SQT$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** In $\triangle PRT$: $\angle PRT+\angle RPT+\angle RTP=180°$: $$40°+95°+\angle RTP=180° \implies \angle RTP=180°-135°$$ **$\angle RTP=45°$** $\angle RTP$ and $\angle STQ$ are vertically opposite angles (PQ and RS intersect at T): $$\angle RTP=\angle STQ=45°$$ In $\triangle STQ$: $\angle STQ+\angle TSQ+\angle SQT=180°$: $$45°+75°+\angle SQT=180° \implies \angle SQT=180°-120°$$ **$\angle SQT=60°$** --- ## Question 23 **Question:** In Fig. 6.43, if $PQ \perp PS$, $PQ \parallel SR$, $\angle SQR=28°$ and $\angle QRT=65°$, find the values of $x$ and $y$. *(3 Marks — Hard)* **Answer** $PQ \perp PS \implies \angle SPQ=90°$. Since $PQ \parallel SR$ and QS is a transversal: $$x=\angle QSR \quad (\text{alternate interior angles, where } x=\angle PQS)$$ Given $\angle SQR=28°$, $\angle QRT=65°$. In $\triangle QSR$, $\angle QRT$ is the exterior angle at R, equal to the sum of the two remote interior angles: $$\angle QSR+\angle SQR=\angle QRT$$ $$\angle QSR+28°=65° \implies \angle QSR=65°-28°=37°$$ **$x=\angle QSR=37°$** In $\triangle SPQ$: $\angle SPQ+\angle PQS+\angle PSQ=180°$: $$90°+x+y=180° \implies 90°+37°+y=180° \implies 127°+y=180°$$ **$y=53°$** --- ## Question 24 **Question:** In Fig. 6.44, side QR of $\triangle PQR$ is produced to point S. The bisectors of $\angle PQR$ and $\angle PRS$ meet at point T. Prove that $\angle QTR=\dfrac12\angle QPR$. *(5 Marks — Hard)* **Answer** We know the exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. In $\triangle PQR$, $\angle PRS$ is the exterior angle at R: $$\angle PRS=\angle QPR+\angle PQR$$ Halving both sides: $$\dfrac12\angle PRS=\dfrac12\angle QPR+\dfrac12\angle PQR$$ Since RT bisects $\angle PRS$ ($\angle TRS=\dfrac12\angle PRS$) and QT bisects $\angle PQR$ ($\angle TQR=\dfrac12\angle PQR$): $$\angle TRS=\dfrac12\angle QPR+\angle TQR \qquad ...(i)$$ Now, in $\triangle TQR$, $\angle TRS$ is the exterior angle at R: $$\angle TRS=\angle QTR+\angle TQR \qquad ...(ii)$$ From (i) and (ii): $$\angle QTR+\angle TQR=\dfrac12\angle QPR+\angle TQR$$ **$\therefore\ \angle QTR=\dfrac12\angle QPR$ — proved.**

## Question 1 **Question:** In Fig. 6.13, lines AB and CD intersect each other at point O. If $\angle AOC+\angle BOE=70°$ and $\angle BOD=40°$, find $\angle BOE$ and reflex $\angle COE$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** $\angle AOC=\angle BOD=40°$ (vertically opposite angles, since AB and CD are two lines intersecting at O). Given $\angle AOC+\angle BOE=70°$: $$40°+\angle BOE=70° \implies \angle BOE=70°-40°$$ **$\angle BOE=30°$** Also, $\angle AOC+\angle COE+\angle BOE=180°$ (AOB is a straight line): $$40°+\angle COE+30°=180° \implies \angle COE=180°-70°=110°$$ Reflex $\angle COE=360°-\angle COE=360°-110°$ **Reflex $\angle COE=250°$** --- ## Question 2 **Question:** In Fig. 6.14, lines XY and MN intersect each other at point O. If $\angle POY=90°$ and $a:b=2:3$, find $c$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** Since $\angle POY=90°$, ray OX and ray OP make $\angle POX=90°$ too (POY and POX are supplementary as XOY is a line). $$a+b=90° \qquad ...(i)$$ Given $a:b=2:3$, let $a=2x°$ and $b=3x°$. From (i): $2x°+3x°=90° \implies 5x°=90° \implies x=18°$ $\therefore\ b=3\times18°=54°$ Now, $b+c=180°$ (MOC is a straight line): $$54°+c=180° \implies c=180°-54°$$ **$c=126°$** --- ## Question 3 **Question:** In Fig. 6.15, $\angle PQR=\angle PRQ$. Prove that $\angle PQS=\angle PRT$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** Given $\angle PQR=\angle PRQ$. To prove: $\angle PQS=\angle PRT$. Ray QP stands on line ST (through S, Q, R, T with SQR and QRT straight): $$\angle PQR+\angle PQS=180° \qquad ...(1)$$ Ray RP stands on the same line: $$\angle PRQ+\angle PRT=180° \qquad ...(2)$$ Adding nothing — instead, from (1) and (2), since both right-hand sides equal 180°: $$\angle PQR+\angle PQS=\angle PRQ+\angle PRT$$ $$\implies \angle PQR+\angle PQS=\angle PQR+\angle PRT \quad (\text{since } \angle PRQ=\angle PQR, \text{ given})$$ **$\therefore\ \angle PQS=\angle PRT$ — proved.** --- ## Question 4 **Question:** In Fig. 6.16, if $x+y=w+z$, then prove that AOB is a straight line. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** Given: $x+y=w+z$. To prove: AOB is a straight line, i.e. $x+y=180°$. Since the four angles $x,y,z,w$ make a complete angle at O: $$x+y+w+z=360° \qquad ...(i)$$ Given $x+y=w+z \qquad ...(ii)$ Substituting (ii) into (i): $(x+y)+(x+y)=360°$ $$2(x+y)=360° \implies x+y=180°$$ Similarly $w+z=180°$ (from (ii)). **Since $x+y=180°$, ray OC and ray OD lie on the same straight line through O with A and B on either side, so AOB is a straight line — proved.** --- ## Question 5 **Question:** In Fig. 6.17, POQ is a straight line. Ray OR is perpendicular to line PQ. OS is another ray lying between rays OP and OR. Prove that $\angle ROS=\dfrac12(\angle QOS-\angle POS)$. *(3 Marks — Hard)* **Answer** Given $\angle QOR=90°$ (since OR $\perp$ PQ), so $\angle POR=90°$ too. From the figure: $\angle ROS=\angle POR-\angle POS$ $$\angle ROS=90°-\angle POS \qquad ...(i)$$ Also: $\angle ROS=\angle QOS-\angle QOR$ $$\angle ROS=\angle QOS-90° \qquad ...(ii)$$ Adding (i) and (ii): $$\angle ROS+\angle ROS=\{90°-\angle POS\}+\{\angle QOS-90°\}$$ $$2\angle ROS=\angle QOS-\angle POS$$ **$\therefore\ \angle ROS=\dfrac12(\angle QOS-\angle POS)$ — proved.** --- ## Question 6 **Question:** It is given that $\angle XYZ=64°$ and XY is produced to point P. Draw a figure from the given information. If ray YQ bisects $\angle ZYP$, find $\angle XYQ$ and reflex $\angle QYP$. *(3 Marks — Moderate)* **Answer** Given $\angle XYZ=64°$. প্ৰশ্ন 16 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.33 ত, PQ আৰু RS দুখন দাপোণ পৰস্পৰ সমান্তৰালকৈ ৰখা হৈছে। AB আপতিত ৰশ্মিয়ে PQ দাপোণৰ B বিন্দুত পৰি প্ৰতিফলিত হৈ BC পথেৰে গৈ RS দাপোণৰ C বিন্দুত পৰিছে। এই ৰশ্মি আকৌ CD দিশে প্ৰতিফলিত হৈছে। প্ৰমাণ কৰা যে $AB \parallel CD$। *(5 নম্বৰ — কঠিন)* **উত্তৰ** চিত্ৰমতে, PQ আৰু RS দুখন সমতল দাপোণ পৰস্পৰ সমান্তৰাল। আপতিত ৰশ্মি AB এ PQ দাপোণত B বিন্দুত পৰি BC ৰশ্মি হিচাপে প্ৰতিফলিত হয়। CD ৰশ্মি RS দাপোণৰ C বিন্দুৰ পৰা প্ৰতিফলিত হৈছে। প্ৰমাণ কৰিব লাগে যে $AB \parallel CD$। আমি জানো, আপতন কোণ = প্ৰতিফলন কোণ। $$\therefore\ \angle 1=\angle 2 \ \text{ আৰু } \ \angle 3=\angle 4 \qquad ...(1)$$ $\angle 1$ হৈছে আপতিত ৰশ্মি AB আৰু অভিলম্ব BL ৰ মাজৰ কোণ; $\angle 2$ হৈছে প্ৰতিফলিত ৰশ্মি BC আৰু অভিলম্ব BL ৰ মাজৰ কোণ। সেইদৰে $\angle 3$ আৰু $\angle 4$ C বিন্দুত থকা আপতন আৰু প্ৰতিফলনৰ সংগতি কোণ। যিহেতু $PQ \parallel RS$ আৰু $BL \perp PQ$, আমি পাওঁ $CM \perp RS$ ও, গতিকে $BL \parallel CM$ (দুয়োটাই সমান্তৰাল ৰেখা যোৰৰ লম্ব)। এতিয়া, $BL \parallel CM$ আৰু BC ছেদক: $$\angle 2=\angle 3 \quad (\text{একান্তৰ অন্তঃকোণ}) \qquad ...(2)$$ $$\angle ABC=\angle 1+\angle 2=\angle 2+\angle 2=2\angle 2 \quad ((1) \text{ ৰ পৰা } \angle 1=\angle 2 \text{ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰি})$$ $$\angle BCD=\angle 3+\angle 4=\angle 3+\angle 3=2\angle 3 \quad ((1) \text{ ৰ পৰা } \angle 3=\angle 4 \text{ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰি})$$ কিন্তু (2) ৰ পৰা, $\angle 2=\angle 3$, গতিকে $2\angle 2=2\angle 3$: $$\therefore\ \angle ABC=\angle BCD$$ $\angle ABC$ আৰু $\angle BCD$ হৈছে ছেদক BC এ বঢ়োৱা AB আৰু CD ৰেখাৰ সৈতে গঠন কৰা একান্তৰ অন্তঃকোণ, আৰু সিহঁত সমান। **$\therefore\ AB \parallel CD$ — প্ৰমাণিত।** --- ## ## প্ৰশ্ন 1 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.13 ত, AB আৰু CD ৰেখা দুডালে O বিন্দুত পৰস্পৰক ছেদ কৰিছে। যদি $\angle AOC+\angle BOE=70°$ আৰু $\angle BOD=40°$, তেন্তে $\angle BOE$ আৰু প্ৰত্যাৱৰ্তী $\angle COE$ নিৰ্ণয় কৰা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** $\angle AOC=\angle BOD=40°$ (বিপ্ৰতীপ কোণ, যিহেতু AB আৰু CD দুডাল ৰেখা O ত ছেদ কৰিছে)। দিয়া আছে $\angle AOC+\angle BOE=70°$: $$40°+\angle BOE=70° \implies \angle BOE=70°-40°$$ **$\angle BOE=30°$** আকৌ, $\angle AOC+\angle COE+\angle BOE=180°$ (AOB এডাল সৰলৰেখা): $$40°+\angle COE+30°=180° \implies \angle COE=180°-70°=110°$$ প্ৰত্যাৱৰ্তী $\angle COE=360°-\angle COE=360°-110°$ **প্ৰত্যাৱৰ্তী $\angle COE=250°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 2 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.14 ত, XY আৰু MN ৰেখা দুডালে O বিন্দুত পৰস্পৰক ছেদ কৰিছে। যদি $\angle POY=90°$ আৰু $a:b=2:3$, তেন্তে $c$ নিৰ্ণয় কৰা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** যিহেতু $\angle POY=90°$, ৰশ্মি OX আৰু OP এ $\angle POX=90°$ ও গঠন কৰিব (POY আৰু POX সম্পূৰক, কাৰণ XOY এডাল ৰেখা)। $$a+b=90° \qquad ...(i)$$ দিয়া আছে $a:b=2:3$, ধৰোঁ $a=2x°$ আৰু $b=3x°$। (i) ৰ পৰা: $2x°+3x°=90° \implies 5x°=90° \implies x=18°$ $\therefore\ b=3\times18°=54°$ এতিয়া, $b+c=180°$ (MOC এডাল সৰলৰেখা): $$54°+c=180° \implies c=180°-54°$$ **$c=126°$** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 3 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.15 ত, $\angle PQR=\angle PRQ$। প্ৰমাণ কৰা যে $\angle PQS=\angle PRT$। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** দিয়া আছে $\angle PQR=\angle PRQ$। প্ৰমাণ কৰিব লাগে যে $\angle PQS=\angle PRT$। ৰশ্মি QP এ ST ৰেখাৰ ওপৰত থিয় হৈছে (S, Q, R, T একে ৰেখাত, SQR আৰু QRT সৰলৰেখা): $$\angle PQR+\angle PQS=180° \qquad ...(1)$$ ৰশ্মি RP এ একে ৰেখাৰ ওপৰত থিয় হৈছে: $$\angle PRQ+\angle PRT=180° \qquad ...(2)$$ (1) আৰু (2) ৰ পৰা, দুয়োটাৰে সোঁফাল $180°$ ৰ সমান বাবে: $$\angle PQR+\angle PQS=\angle PRQ+\angle PRT$$ $$\implies \angle PQR+\angle PQS=\angle PQR+\angle PRT \quad (\text{যিহেতু } \angle PRQ=\angle PQR, \text{ দিয়া আছে})$$ **$\therefore\ \angle PQS=\angle PRT$ — প্ৰমাণিত।** --- ## প্ৰশ্ন 4 **প্ৰশ্ন:** চিত্ৰ 6.16 ত, যদি $x+y=w+z$, তেন্তে প্ৰমাণ কৰা যে AOB এডাল সৰলৰেখা। *(3 নম্বৰ — মধ্যম)* **উত্তৰ** দিয়া আছে: $x+y=w+z$। প্ৰমাণ কৰিব লাগে: AOB এডাল সৰলৰেখা, অৰ্থাৎ $x+y=180°$। যিহেতু $x,y,z,w$ চাৰিটা কোণে O ত এটা সম্পূৰ্ণ কোণ গঠন কৰে: $$x+y+w+z=360° \qquad ...(i)$$ দিয়া আছে $x+y=w+z \qquad ...(ii)$ (ii) ক (i) ত প্ৰতিস্থাপন কৰি: $(x+y)+(x+y)=360°$ $$2(x+y)=360° \implies x+y=180°$$ সেইদৰে $w+z=180°$ ((ii) ৰ পৰা)। **যিহেতু $x+y=180°$, ৰশ্মি OC আৰু OD O ৰ মাজেৰে যোৱা একেডাল সৰলৰেখাত থাকে, A আৰু B দুয়োফালে থাকি, গতিকে AOB এডাল সৰলৰেখা — প্ৰমাণিত।** --- ##
